To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TPL N-domain is active on long chain triacylglycerols (TG) and stabilized by colipase.
the N-Terminal domain of Turkey Pancreas Lipase is active on long chain triacylglycerols, and is stabilized by Colipase.
the N-Terminal Domain (N-TPL) of turkey pancreatic lipase (TPL) was expressed in the methylotrophic yeast P. pastoris, purified to homogeneity and characterized for its activity on long chain TG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of the turkey pancreatic lipase (TPL) N-terminal domain (amino acid residues 1-300) fused with a histidine tail in Pichia Pastoris.
the first description of a functional N-terminal domain of turkey lipase that can hydrolyse insolube long chain TG, and that is stabilized in the presence of colipase.
the characterization of a novel enzyme, the turkey pancreatic lipase N-terminal domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal domain of turkey pancreatic lipase is a functional and active lipase domain, able to catalyse TG hydrolysis, but with a very low stability at the lipid–water interface.
the N-T-terminal domain of TPL has a specific activity towards insoluble substrates and its activity can be enhanced by colipase.
the N-Terminal Domain is active on long chain triglycerides and stabilized by colipase, and therefore it is a potential tool in the design of a new enzyme for the hydrolysis of TG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were successful in the expression of the N-TPL domain in P. pastoris, which was purified and characterized.
the N-Terminal domain of Turkey pancreatic lipase is active on long chain triacylglycerols.
the N-terminal domain of TPL, despite the absence of its C-terminal domain, has a catalytic activity on long chain TG, and is stabilized by colipase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N-TPL can be used as a model for the TPL N-terminus to study the structure and function of this region.
the N-terminal domain of TPL has a specific activity on long chain TG, and that this activity is stabilized by colipase.
the N-Ter domain of TPL is active on long chain TG and stabilized by colipase.
